lessons.title: Review — the four stem changes, all of them
lessons.gloss: review — the stem-change system, now complete, and the one pattern with a single member

segments.text: Nothing new in this chapter. Say a verb whose stem breaks under stress — any one you have met.
Something finished in the last two chapters and it is worth stopping for.

Spanish has four stem-change patterns. Not five, not a dozen — four. You met the first two long ago with querer and poder, and the last two in the chapters you have just finished. That is the whole system, and you now hold all of it:

utterances: the change: e becomes ie. the verb that taught it: querer. what breaks: becomes quiero.
the change: o becomes ue. the verb that taught it: poder. what breaks: becomes puedo.
the change: e becomes i. the verb that taught it: conseguir. what breaks: becomes consigo.
the change: u becomes ue. the verb that taught it: jugar. what breaks: becomes juego.

segments.text: This table is allowed here because every row in it is something you can already do. It is a picture of the ground you hold, not a list to memorise.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the pattern with one member

segments.text: The fourth row is strange, and worth knowing precisely.
u becomes ue happens in exactly one verb in the entire language: jugar.

Not "mostly one." One. Every other Spanish verb with a u in its stem leaves it alone. So you are not learning a pattern here so much as a single fact with a pattern's shape — which is easier, not harder, and is the kind of thing a course should tell you instead of letting you brace for more.

segments.instruction: one verb from each of the four rows
segments.source: [YOU SAY: one verb from each of the four rows]

segments.instruction: the four changes themselves, as sounds — e-ie, o-ue, e-i, u-ue
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the four changes themselves, as sounds — *e-ie, o-ue, e-i, u-ue*]

segments.text: Until naming the pattern is faster than working it out.

segments.prompt: How many stem-change patterns does Spanish have in total?

feedback.correct: Four — and you now hold all of them.

segments.prompt: Which pattern belongs to exactly one verb, and which verb?

feedback.correct: Yes — jugar is the only u-ue verb in Spanish.
feedback.incorrect: u to ue, and the verb is jugar. It is the only one.

segments.text: How many stem-change patterns are there? (Four — and that is all of them.) Which one has a single member? (u becomes ue, only jugar.) Next chapter is not about forms at all — it is about three places where English gives you one word and Spanish makes you choose.
